title: Microferry traffic-split protocol and ops crib notes
content:
Context:
This is a working notes + checklist for the 'microferry' rollout approach: move tiny increments of user traffic between model/runtime variants using short-lived traffic ferry lanes rather than big cohort flips. Goal is more atomicity for risky changes (kernel swap, quantization change, kv-cache behavior) while keeping latency surface stable.

Summary of approach:
- Ferry lanes: create ephemeral traffic lanes that take N requests/sec (or X%) for 5-20 minutes, then fold back or escalate.
- Atomicity: each lane targets a single runtime change (e.g., new kernel selection) so we can attribute regressions easily.
- Observability-first: each lane has tailored alerts and golden-signature prompts sampled at 100% for the lane.

Rollout calendar (high-level - local timezone PDT):
- 2026-05-20 09:00 - Preflight smoke + canary deployment (0% traffic -> 0.1%)
- 2026-05-20 09:10 - Microferry lane A (0.5% traffic) 09:10-09:30
- 2026-05-20 09:35 - Microferry lane B (1.0% traffic) 09:35-09:55
- 2026-05-20 10:10 - Microferry lane C (2.5% traffic) 10:10-10:40
- 2026-05-20 11:00 - Decision point: scale to 5% / hold / rollback
- 2026-05-20 12:00 - Post-rollout telemetry digest and short retro

Preflight checklist (must clear before any lane spins up):
- [ ] PRs merged: list linked PR(s) and verify CI green (see github link above).
- [ ] Smoke images deployed to staging and pass smoke-suite (smoke tag: mf/2026-05-20).
- [ ] Latency budget baseline captured (p50/p95/p99 for last 24h).
- [ ] Golden prompts updated and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood/release/microferry/golden-2026-05-20.json
- [ ] Pager on-call assigned (primary: Diego, secondary: Aisha).
- [ ] Rollback package prepared and tested (scripts + cloud runbook).
- [ ] Customer-impact list checked for any scheduled marketing / demos in rollout window.

Spin-up steps for lane (operators):
1) Create ferry lane flag in rollout service: POST /rollout/lanes {name: mf-a, capacity: 0.5%}
2) Attach variant tag to lane (model: open-vm-v2-kernelB, route: text-gen-prod)
3) Start sampling golden prompts to lane; ensure 100% of golden goes to lane for exact diff.
4) Wait 3 minutes for warmed instances, check per-instance GPU mem / kv cache heat map.
5) Open lane to user traffic (increase to target) via control plane.

Observability checks (immediate + rolling):
- Synthetic/golden checks (every 30s): compare new vs baseline for: latency p50/p95, hallucination rate (simple classifier), embedding drift score.
- Metric thresholds to fail fast (5m window):
  - error_rate_new_lane > baseline_error_rate + 0.4% -> FAIL
  - p95_latency_new_lane > baseline_p95 * 1.25 -> FAIL
  - token_loss_ratio spike > 0.5% -> FAIL
- Slow degradation pattern: if sustained small deltas across 3 lanes escalate to hold.
- Smoke traces: sampling of request traces; look for k/v cache miss storms, kernel fallback logs, OOMs.

Alert queries (examples for console):
- Errors: sum(rate(request_errors[5m])) by lane > 5 -> page oncall
- Latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, lane))
- Golden-test diff: count(golden_mismatch{lane=~"mf-.*"}) > 0 -> attach failure stack and most-recent-golden-output to pager message

Decision matrix (during each decision point):
- All green: proceed to next lane or scale percent by +2x (capped at 5%).
- Minor warnings (single metric violation but no errors): pause for 15m, collect extra samples, escalate to eng if unresolved.
- Hard fail (errors/OOps/ > threshold): immediate rollback of lane and revert control-plane flag, open rollback runbook.

Rollback quick steps (if triggered):
- Step 0: mark lane suspended in control plane (prevent new traffic).
- Step 1: route existing in-flight to fallback variant (force-fallback header).
- Step 2: revert config via infra script (./infra/rollback/microferry-revert.sh mf-a) and close lane.
- Step 3: collect forensic artifacts: top 50 traces, pod logs, kernel trace, baseline comparison artifacts.
- Step 4: notify stakeholders (customers list + product) with templated message (see linked artifacts).

Post-rollout notes to collect (templates):
- Latency delta table: p50/p95/p99 baseline vs new (CSV)
- Cost delta: tokens/sec cost estimate after kernel swap (estimate in spreadsheet)
- Failures observed and root cause hypoth (investigation owners)
- Recommended follow-ups (perf tuning, kernel revert, config guardrails)

Draft release notes snippet (short form for release email / changelog):
- Title: Improve kernel selection for open-vm models (microferry trial)
- Summary: Introduces a new kernel path optimized for short sequences; trialed via microferry traffic lanes to validate latency/cost impact with minimal user exposure.
- Notes for users: No action required. Some short-lived requests during the trial may have marginal latency variance. If you observe degraded responses, please contact support and include request-id header.
- Rollout status: partial (under monitoring)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Q: should golden-test sampling be 100% or 10x frequency but lower volume? tradeoff between signal and synthetic noise.
- Q: add explicit per-customer opt-out for enterprise customers during microferry lanes? legal/contract check.
- TODO: automate lane creation from template; current step is manual and error-prone (MICROFERRY-CLI ticket).
- TODO: validate that KV cache warm-up script covers both new kernel and old kernel eviction patterns.

Slack pointers during rollout (operator script):
- channel: #release-ops (use format: [mf-a] 09:12 -> open to 0.5%)
- pager message template: "mf-lane {name} FAIL: {metric} exceeded threshold at {time}. Rolling back. Runbook: <link>"

Notes-to-self style: small, messy - this doc is a working runbook. Decision points should be recorded in the rollcall log and pasted into the permanent release brief. Keep this pattern lightweight - microferry lanes succeed only if operator burden is minimal.

Appendix: quick commands
- Create lane (example): curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/rollout/lanes -d '{\"name\":\"mf-a\",\"percent\":0.5,\"variant\":\"open-vm-v2-kernelB\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPKEY'
- Pause lane: curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/rollout/lanes/mf-a/pause
- Rollback script: ./tools/rollback-mf.sh mf-a --collect-logs=true

If anything is unclear ping Diego or @release-ops in slack. I'll iterate this after the first run and fold into the canonical runbook if the pattern holds.

-- Claire
